title: QuickStrike: compact autosurge card for Dedicated capacity ops
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Summary:
Design a compact, embeddable UI card (QuickStrike) for Redwood Console that lets operators view GPU pool health and perform fast autosurge/burst operations without leaving list or pipeline screens. The card should be low-visual-weight, keyboard-accessible, and optimized for frequent ops flows (on-call, runbook actions).

Problem:
Operators need a fast path to react to short latency spikes or traffic surges. Current dedicated capacity dashboards require three clicks and a context switch to configure burst amounts or to see recommended autoscaling adjustments. This increases mean time to mitigate and leads to overprovisioning.

Goals:
- Surface essential health signals (latency vs SLO, queue depth, %usable GPUs, thermal throttling flag) in a 320x220 card footprint.
- Provide a single control for temporary burst (QuickBurst slider + preset buttons) and an opt-in autosurge toggle with recommended parameters.
- Show clear cost delta estimate for applied burst and ability to preview the resulting SLO impact.
- Keep interaction simple: preview -> confirm -> apply. Include an undo affordance for 2 minutes.
- Fit into existing fleet list rows and pool detail sidebars.

Constraints & considerations:
- Backend telemetry: needs a new aggregate endpoint from ENG:ENG-4219 that returns 1m/5m latency percentiles, queue length, and available burst credits per pool. Frontend must gracefully degrade to last-known-values when telemetry is delayed.
- Safety: API must enforce max burst ceiling per pool (ENG-4388). Design must reflect hard limits and temporary errors.
- Multi-tenant: some pools have restricted burst permissions; CTA should be disabled with explicit reason and link to RBAC docs.
- Cost estimation is approximate; UI must label as estimate and link to cost center breakdown.

Proposed components inside the card:
- Compact header: pool name, small health dot (green/yellow/red), last-updated timestamp.
- Health row (icons + microcopy): 99th latency, queue depth, GPU utilization, thermal flag.
- QuickBurst control: slider (0-100% of pool burst budget) + three micro-presets (10%, 30%, 60%). Numeric input inline for precision.
- Autosurge toggle: brief explainer with recommended threshold (e.g., auto-scale up when 95th latency > X ms). Tapping opens a micro-dialog with advanced options.
- Cost preview: inline badge with delta/month and delta/hour as small numbers; hover or chevron expands to a 2-line tooltip showing tokenized assumptions.
- CTA row: Apply (primary) / Preview only (secondary) / Undo toast on apply.

User flows:
1) On-call operator sees a spike; opens pool row actions -> QuickStrike card. Adjusts QuickBurst to 30% -> presses Apply -> sees confirmation toast with ETA and undo.
2) Platform engineer wants to enable safe autosurge for a pool. Opens card, toggles Autosurge -> micro-dialog shows recommended thresholds -> saves -> deck logs rollout entry for audit.

Accessibility and micro-interactions:
- All controls keyboard-focusable, slider supports arrow keys and page up/down.
- Color is not sole signal; health icons include text and ARIA labels.
- Confirmation flows readable by screen readers; undo button in toast focused on open.

Prototype links and files:
- Figma (live prototype): https://www.figma.com/file/ExampleQuickStrikePrototype
- Clickable prototype (flows): https://www.figma.com/proto/ExampleQuickStrikeFlow
- Design system tokens used: token list in Drive (link below).

Metrics of success:
- Reduce median time-to-burst from list view from 90s to <30s in playtest.
- 25% fewer full-pool page navigations in ops sessions.
- No increase in accidental burst activations after adding undo affordance.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Full feature parity vs brevity: the card intentionally omits deep configuration (rate limits, node-level controls); deep ops remain in pool detail page.
- Cost vs speed: showing estimated cost might discourage use; we emphasize quick preview and tie to cost center drilldown rather than burying numbers.

comments: 2025-02-12 Lina Chen: Initial draft and wireframes added to Figma. Marked estimate 5 points after tech sync.
2025-02-14 Aisha Kapoor (PM): Prefer explicit cost preview. Added request to show delta/hour and delta/month. Please surface RBAC state when disabled.

2025-02-20 Marco Velasquez (Eng): Reviewed constraints. ENG-4219 will provide latency and queue endpoints by 2025-02-28. Need to confirm API shape for burst credits. Backend will return a 'max_burst_pct' field.
2025-02-25 Design review: Reduced microcopy, moved 'last updated' to header, added undo toast. Accessibility pair review scheduled 2025-02-27.
2025-03-03 Marco Velasquez: Updated prototype to include disabled states and cost tooltip. Requesting UX copy pass from PM and acceptance criteria confirmation.
decisions: Keep card compact; omit node-level controls and full autoscale policy editor from card (deeper config on pool detail).
Include undo toast for applied bursts with 2-minute window.
Show cost estimate as an explicit preview badge and link to detailed cost breakdown (no hard numbers in microcopy).
acceptance_criteria: QuickStrike card renders in fleet list rows and pool detail sidebar at 320x220 without layout regression.
QuickBurst slider updates preview cost and respects backend 'max_burst_pct' ceilings.
Autosurge toggle opens micro-dialog with recommended thresholds and saves to pool settings via console API.
Apply flow shows confirmation toast with undo, and undo reverts the burst within 2 minutes.
Telemetry fallbacks show 'last known' timestamp when live metrics are unavailable.
